article_context: The body image introduces practical recommendations for preparing a self-leveling floor before tiling, emphasizing careful inspection of the prepared substrate and correctly laid tilework.
image_reading: An overhead view shows exactly one kneeling worker facing a partially tiled floor.
Installed square tiles and grout lines occupy the upper area; exposed combed adhesive and bare substrate remain visible below.
A detached trowel lies separately on the adhesive area to the worker's right, while red alignment guides cross the floor.
The worker's head, shoulders, and torso can support a small inspection shift, but no active tool contact or laying motion is clearly established.

models.positive_prompt: The kneeling worker makes one measured inspection shift of his head, shoulders, and torso over the prepared floor, with his arms staying away from the detached trowel at right. Keep the camera fixed and the tiles, adhesive, substrate, grout lines, and red guides rigid; by the end he settles into a slightly adjusted inspection posture with both worker and trowel continuously visible.
models.scene_plan: Over five seconds, use a single fixed overhead shot. The worker immediately begins one moderate, low-risk inspection shift: his head angles slightly toward the tile edge while his shoulders and torso lean subtly with it, then the movement eases into a clearly adjusted kneeling posture near the final frames. His arms do not reach toward any tool. The detached trowel remains separate at right, and every floor region and guide stays rigid.

structured_intent.attention_anchor: The visible worker's head, shoulders, and torso inspecting the floor
structured_intent.editorial_meaning: Careful inspection of a prepared, level substrate supports reliable tile installation.
structured_intent.feasibility_assessment: The kneeling worker and his inspection orientation are visible, but no active adhesive application, tile placement, hand-to-tool contact, or safe tool trajectory is proven. A single low-risk upper-body inspection shift is feasible while the work surface remains locked.
structured_intent.geometry_invariant: The detached trowel remains lying separately at right; installed tiles, grout grid, adhesive ridges, substrate boundaries, and red alignment guides retain their rigid geometry.
structured_intent.identity_invariant: Exactly one visible worker and one detached trowel remain present; the worker keeps the same limbs and clothing, and no tiles, tools, or floor elements appear or disappear.
structured_intent.initial_state: One worker kneels with his back to the camera and faces the boundary between installed tiles, combed adhesive, and bare substrate; a detached trowel lies separately to his right.
structured_intent.motion_boundary: Only the worker's head, shoulders, and torso may make one inspection shift; his arms stay away from the trowel, while the camera, trowel, adhesive, substrate, installed tiles, grout lines, walls, window, and red guides remain source-locked.
structured_intent.primary_action: The worker makes one small upper-body shift while inspecting the prepared floor.
structured_intent.semantic_invariant: The worker remains focused on inspecting floor preparation for tile installation through the final frame.
structured_intent.terminal_state: The worker settles into a slightly adjusted kneeling inspection posture without touching the detached trowel or changing the floor.
